comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation supports emotional wellness through global Employee Assistance Programs offering 12 free in-person counseling sessions and unlimited phone consultations, along with comprehensive time-away policies, caregiving benefits, and a paid Global Sabbatical Program for teammates with at least 15 years of continuous service.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Bank of America provide comprehensive wellness frameworks that include sabbatical programs and time-away policies, but differ in structure and specificity. Goldman Sachs explicitly mandates a minimum 15-day annual vacation for all employees and offers unpaid sabbaticals for long-tenured staff, focusing on work-life balance metrics. Bank of America also offers a paid Global Sabbatical Program for employees with at least 15 years of service and emphasizes emotional wellness through Employee Assistance Programs (counseling sessions) alongside general caregiving benefits, without specifying a minimum vacation day count.

sentences.text: We provide a number of policies for our employees that support taking time away from the office when needed, including a minimum of 20 weeks of parental leave and up to four weeks of family care leave in order to assist with the care of family members with a serious health condition, death of an immediate family member or miscarriage, in addition to bereavement leave.
We allow managing directors to take time off without a fixed vacation day entitlement, and have also set a minimum annual expected vacation usage of 15 days for all employees.
For longer-tenured employees, we offer an unpaid sabbatical leave.
We also recognize the importance of emotional wellness.
The Corporation also offers comprehensive time-away policies and caregiving benefits.
Globally, teammates celebrating at least 15 years of continuous service with the Corporation can participate in our paid Global Sabbatical Program.

sentences.text: We recognize that for our people to be successful in the workplace they need support in their personal, as well as their professional, lives and that is why our wellness framework is designed to promote health and fitness, resilience, and work-life balance.

We provide a number of policies for our employees that support taking time away from the office when needed, including a minimum of 20 weeks of parental leave and up to four weeks of family care leave in order to assist with the care of family members with a serious health condition, death of an immediate family member or miscarriage, in addition to bereavement leave.
We allow managing directors to take time off without a fixed vacation day entitlement, and have also set a minimum annual expected vacation usage of 15 days for all employees.

JPMorganChase offers extensive benefits and wellness packages to support employees and their families, which vary depending on location and include healthcare coverage, retirement benefits, life and disability insurance, access to on-site health and wellness centers, counseling and resources related to mental health, time away policies, child care access and support, tuition assistance, and financial coaching.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company supports the physical, mental, and financial wellbeing of its global workforce and their families through various programs focusing on awareness, prevention, and access. Offerings vary by location but include health care, insurance benefits, mental health resources, flexible work schedules, family leave, child and elder care resources, financial help for fertility/adoption/surrogacy, tuition assistance, and on-site services like health centers and fitness centers.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley offer wellness frameworks that include family leave and mental health support, but Morgan Stanley provides a broader list of specific financial and care resources in this disclosure. Goldman Sachs specifies 20 weeks of parental leave and up to four weeks of family care leave. Morgan Stanley lists 'family leave' generally alongside specific financial assistance for fertility, adoption, and surrogacy, as well as on-site mental health counseling and fitness centers, whereas Goldman Sachs focuses on leave durations and minimum vacation usage.
